result.title: Non-penetrating World Models
result.summary: We study a new problem of preventing object penetration in interactive video world models. To understand how existing models handle this, we introduce NoPeBench, a benchmark that evaluates how world models respond to physical obstacles. Our evaluation reveals that none of the open-source models can reliably prevent such failures. Surprisingly, however, these models already encode the information needed to predict such violations. We find that the hidden states of diffusion transformers (DiTs) can predict whether a candidate action will penetrate an obstacle. Building on this, we introduce NoPeWorld, a lightweight framework that detects and prevents penetration. Specifically, we train a small prediction head on top of a frozen DiT's hidden states to read out if a candidate action is safe or not. Unsafe actions are then replaced with safe ones that best preserve the original intent. Despite its simplicity, NoPeWorld substantially reduces the physical violation rate, averaged over six video world models, from 74% to 16%. Remarkably, our method shows zero-shot generalization to open-domain imagery, third-person viewpoints, and moving obstacles. We publicly release our code, the NoPeBench benchmark, and model weights. Project Page: https://nopeworld.github.io .

AI.brief_summary: 论文研究交互式视频世界模型中的物体穿透问题，提出 NoPeBench 基准评估各模型对物理障碍的响应，并给出 NoPeWorld：在冻结 DiT 的隐状态上训练小型预测头判断候选动作是否安全，再用安全动作替换，平均将违规率从 74% 降至 16%。
AI.relevance_reason: 「冻结骨干隐状态探针 + 候选动作安全判定与替换」可供核查 LVR 中 latent 是否确实编码任务必要的视觉证据、以及能否据读出结果筛选或校正推理路径，但该工作属视频世界模型，与 VLM 推理主线并不直接对应。
